subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

To be on thin ice

options.text: To be in a risky situation

solution:
The correct answer is "**To be in a risky situation".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** Here let's see what the given idiom means with the help of an example:

__
 
• To be on thin ice - To be doing something very risky that could result in imminent disaster or ruin.
 
 
• Eg. I hope you realize that you'll be on thin ice if you decide to gamble your employees' retirement funds on such a dodgy investment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here we will learn about more such idioms:

 
• Be on the last legs - Of a machine, to be near a complete breakdown or loss of functionality.
 
 
• Eg. Judging by all that noise coming from her car, I'm pretty sure it's on its last legs.
 
 
 
• Be on the case - To be constantly nagging, harassing, or annoying someone.
 
 
• Eg. My boss has been on my case all week to get that report done
